question: If I work while I'm incarcerated, in a prison job or on work release, how is my pay set, what can the state deduct from my earnings and in what order, and what do I get back when I'm released?

gold_sections.why: Prison-job pay: a daily allowance set by the Director that accumulates and is paid at discharge, with a Director-set portion drawable while inside.
State work release: pay equal to regular employees, wages paid to the Director, the four-step order of deductions, and where the balance goes.
Mandatory 10 percent set-aside of all funds into a personal trust account until it reaches $1,000; paid out on parole or final discharge.
Release payment: all accumulated allowance and bonus funds after eight months served, a discretionary top-up to twenty-five dollars, transportation and clothing.

Paying court-imposed fines, costs and restitution in full or by payment plan is a condition of any work program; missed payments can end participation; the Director withholds those payments from amounts due; child-support placement preference.
Prison jobs run with a public or private entity: Director arranges pay, receives the wages and deducts, in order, support, court debt and a portion of keep; balance credited under 53.1-42.
Director may set up pay incentives and bonuses for responsible or exemplary work.

Program assignments: the Director may set pay incentives by difficulty and level of effort (E); refusing an assignment costs good conduct and earned sentence credits (D); inmates employed under Article 2 are not state employees and get no state-personnel, unemployment or workers' compensation benefits (F).

Subsection B repeats the work-release payment condition and sets a five-step priority that puts restitution ahead of fines and costs; subsection C gives credit against fines and costs for work while incarcerated.
The fifty-dollar work release fee that 53.1-60 includes among the work-release expenses deducted from wages.

Department pre-release work release or community programs for nonviolent prisoners within six months of release: wages to the program after payroll deductions, distributed for keep, travel, dependents and court debts; balance paid on release.
Court orders or judgments against a state prisoner are satisfied from the inmate trust account to the extent possible.
On request of social services, the Director withholds part of a work-releasee's earnings for dependents on public assistance.
Local (jail) work release, which also governs state felons held in jail and state prisoners placed in local programs: distribution purposes and balance paid on release.
The Virginia Minimum Wage Act's definition of employee excludes people confined in a penal or corrective institution.

nuggets.text: A state prisoner is credited (allowed) an amount the Director of the Department of Corrections sets for each day of labor satisfactory to the superintendent or sheriff in charge; the allowance accumulates and is paid to the prisoner at discharge, except a portion the Director lets the prisoner draw on while confined.
nuggets.quote: shall be allowed an amount to be established by the Director for each day of labor satisfactory to the superintendent or sheriff in whose charge he is. The allowance so made shall accumulate and be paid over to the prisoner upon discharge, except that an amount thereof to be determined by the Director may be drawn upon by the prisoner

nuggets.text: The Director may set up pay incentives, including a bonus for prisoners in positions of responsibility or who perform their jobs in an exemplary manner.
nuggets.quote: Such system may provide for the payment of a bonus to any prisoner who is assigned to employment in any position of responsibility or who performs his job in an exemplary manner.

nuggets.text: Virginia's minimum wage law does not treat a person confined in a state or local penal or corrective institution as an employee.
nuggets.quote: Any person confined in any penal or corrective institution of the Commonwealth or any of its political subdivisions

nuggets.text: On state work release, the Director arranges the pay, which must be the same as regular employees in similar occupations, and the wages are paid to the Director rather than to the prisoner.
nuggets.quote: The compensation for such employment shall be arranged by the Director and shall be the same as that of regular employees in similar occupations. Any wages earned shall be paid to the Director.

nuggets.text: The Director deducts from state work-release wages in a fixed order: (1) any judicial or administrative support order; (2) court-ordered fines, restitution or costs; (3) travel and other expenses made necessary by the work release, including the work release fee in 53.1-150; (4) the prisoner's keep. The balance is credited to the prisoner's account or sent to the prisoner's family, in whatever amount the prisoner chooses.
nuggets.quote: 1. Meet the obligation of any judicial or administrative order to provide support and such funds shall be disbursed according to the terms of such order; 2. Pay any fines, restitution or costs as ordered by the court; 3. Pay travel and other such expenses made necessary by his work release employment or participation in an educational or rehabilitative program, including the sums specified in § 53.1-150 ; and 4. Defray the prisoner's keep. The balance shall be credited to the prisoner's account or sent to his family in an amount the prisoner so chooses.

nuggets.text: In a prison work program the Director runs with a public or private entity, wages are paid to the Director, who deducts in order (1) any judicial or administrative support order, (2) court-ordered fines, restitution or costs, and (3) a portion of the prisoner's keep, and credits the balance to the prisoner's account under 53.1-42.
nuggets.quote: Wages earned by prisoners shall be paid to the Director who shall deduct from such wages, in the following order of priority, an amount to: 1. Meet the obligation of any judicial or administrative order to provide support and such funds shall be disbursed according to the terms of such order; 2. Pay any fines, restitution or costs as ordered by the court; and 3. Defray a portion of the prisoner's keep. The balance shall be credited to the prisoner's account in accordance with § 53.1-42

nuggets.text: Under the court-payment statute, money withheld from a work-release participant goes to support orders first, then restitution, and only then to fines or costs, before work expenses and keep.
nuggets.quote: 2. Pay any restitution as ordered by the court; 3. Pay any fines or costs as ordered by the court;

nuggets.text: A prisoner who owes court-imposed fines, costs, forfeitures, restitution or penalties must, as a condition of any work program, pay them in full or under an agreed installment or deferred payment plan; missing agreed payments can end the prisoner's work-program participation until the debts are paid, and the Director withholds the payments from any amounts due to the prisoner.
nuggets.quote: he shall be required as a condition of participating in any work program to either make full payment or make payments in accordance with an agreed upon installment or deferred payment plan while participating in such work program. If, after the person enters into an installment or deferred payment agreement, the person fails to pay as agreed, his participation in the work program may be terminated until all fines, costs, forfeitures, restitution and penalties are satisfied. The Director shall withhold such payments from any amounts due to such person.

nuggets.text: Work done while incarcerated on or after July 1, 2023, at a wage below the Virginia minimum wage earns credit toward court fines and costs at the same rate as community service work, minus any wages received.
nuggets.quote: a person who is performing work while incarcerated shall be credited at the same rate as the community service work rate less any wages received. As used in this subsection, "work performed while incarcerated" means any work done on or after July 1, 2023, by a person confined in any local, regional, or state correctional facility who is paid a wage that is less than the Virginia minimum wage

nuggets.text: A work release participant must pay a fifty-dollar fee as a condition of work release, unless the sentencing/supervision fee was already assessed.
nuggets.quote: Except when the fee referenced in subsection A has been previously assessed, any person (i) who is granted parole or (ii) who participates in a work release program pursuant to the provisions of §§ 53.1-60 and 53.1-131 shall be required to pay a fee of fifty dollars as a condition of parole or work release

nuggets.text: Except for people sentenced to death, life without parole, or a term making them ineligible for release before age 75 (not counting geriatric conditional release), the Department deposits 10 percent of any money an inmate receives, from any source, into a personal trust account until it reaches $1,000.
nuggets.quote: 10 percent of any funds received by an inmate from any source shall be deposited by the Department in the inmate's personal trust account until the account has a balance of $1,000.

nuggets.text: When a prisoner who has served at least eight months is released, the Director must give the prisoner all allowance and bonus funds (53.1-42 and 53.1-43) accumulated and not withdrawn.
nuggets.quote: upon the release of a prisoner who has served at least eight months, shall give the prisoner all funds accumulated to his credit pursuant to §§ 53.1-42 and 53.1-43 and not withdrawn by him

nuggets.text: If those funds total less than twenty-five dollars, the Director may add money so the prisoner has at least twenty-five dollars at release, may provide transportation (to the county or city of commitment or another approved point) on request, and may furnish suitable clothing.
nuggets.quote: the Director may add sufficient money from the appropriation to the Department to enable the prisoner to have a minimum of twenty-five dollars available for withdrawal by him at the time of his release. The Director also may provide such person upon his request with transportation to the county or city where he was committed, or to such other point in the Commonwealth as may be approved by the Director. Such person may also be furnished suitable clothing.

nuggets.text: The money in the personal trust account is paid to the inmate upon parole or final discharge.
nuggets.quote: Funds in an inmate's personal trust account shall be paid to the inmate upon parole or final discharge.

nuggets.text: In the Department's pre-release work release or community program for nonviolent prisoners (within six months of release), any balance of the prisoner's wages left at the end of the sentence is paid to the prisoner upon release.
nuggets.quote: Any balance at the end of his sentence shall be paid to the prisoner upon his release.

office.value: Director of the Department of Corrections sets the prison work allowance, arranges work-release and partner work-program pay, and receives those wages

ordered_list.item: State work release (53.1-60 C): judicial or administrative support orders
State work release: court-ordered fines, restitution or costs (restitution ahead of fines and costs under 19.2-354 B)
State work release: travel and other work-release expenses, including the work release fee
State work release: defray the prisoner's keep
State work release: balance to the prisoner's account or to family, as the prisoner chooses
Prison work program with a public or private entity (53.1-45.1 C): judicial or administrative support orders
Prison work program with a public or private entity: court-ordered fines, restitution or costs
Prison work program with a public or private entity: a portion of the prisoner's keep
Prison work program with a public or private entity: balance credited to the prisoner's allowance account

amount.value: 10 percent of all funds received goes to the personal trust account until it holds $1,000
release top-up to a minimum of twenty-five dollars (discretionary)

fee.value: fifty dollars work release fee, unless the sentencing/supervision fee was already assessed

answer: A prison job earns a daily allowance the Corrections Director sets [N1]; bonuses are possible [N2]; minimum wage law excludes prisoners [N3]. In work programs run with a public or private partner, the Director deducts support orders, then court fines, restitution or costs, then part of your keep, crediting the rest to your account [N6]. Work-release pay must match regular employees in similar jobs but goes to the Director [N4], who deducts, in order: support orders; court fines, restitution and costs; work expenses, including a fifty-dollar fee unless a sentencing/supervision fee was already assessed [N10]; and keep, then sends the rest to your account or family, as you choose [N5]. Another statute puts restitution before fines and costs [N7]. Paying court debts, fully or by plan, is a condition of any work program; missed payments can end it, and the Director withholds payments from money due you [N8]. Prison work paid under minimum wage also earns credit against fines and costs at the community service rate, minus wages [N9]. Ten percent of all money you receive goes to a personal trust account until it holds $1,000 (unless your sentence bars release before 75) [N11], paid out at parole or final discharge [N14]. Your allowance is paid at discharge, minus withdrawals [N1]; after eight months served the Director must also hand over all unwithdrawn allowance and bonus funds [N12] and may top you up to twenty-five dollars, with transportation and clothing [N13]. Pre-release work-release balances are paid at release [N15].

local_option: Sheriffs and regional jail superintendents run local work release (53.1-131) and jail industry programs (53.1-133.4: the sheriff sets the daily allowance and total deductions may not exceed eighty percent of gross wages) and may charge up to $3 a day toward keep (53.1-131.3); state prisoners placed in a local work release program follow the local program's rules (53.1-60 E).
notes: Scope is state prisoners (Department of Corrections). Three deduction orders exist. 53.1-60 C (state work release): support; fines, restitution or costs; travel and work expenses including 53.1-150 sums; keep; balance to account or family. 19.2-354 B (work release under 53.1-60, 53.1-131, 53.1-131.1, 53.1-131.2): support; restitution; fines or costs; travel and expenses; keep; it splits restitution ahead of fines and costs, otherwise matching 53.1-60 C. 53.1-45.1 C (prison work programs run with a public or private entity): support; fines, restitution or costs; a portion of keep; balance credited under 53.1-42. Two further work-release routes list distribution 'purposes' starting with keep (keep; travel and expenses; dependents' support or social-services payments; fines, restitution or costs), without the phrase 'order of priority', and pay any balance to the prisoner on release: local work release under 53.1-131 (covered by 19.2-354 B) and the Department's pre-release program under 53.1-155.1 (nonviolent prisoners sentenced to at least three years, within six months of release; wages go to the program after standard payroll deductions; not named in 19.2-354 B). Release payments: 53.1-42 pays the accumulated allowance at discharge with no time threshold; 53.1-190 adds an express duty, for anyone who served at least eight months, to pay all unwithdrawn 53.1-42 and 53.1-43 funds, plus the discretionary twenty-five-dollar top-up, transportation and clothing. 53.1-43.1 also lets an inmate deposit more into the personal trust account at any time and, once it exceeds $1,000, move the excess to another account, but the balance may not fall below $1,000; once it reaches $1,000, new funds go to the other account. 53.1-41 B's withholding reaches 'any amounts due' to the person. 53.1-41 A gives placement preference to prisoners who assign at least 50 percent of earnings to child support. 53.1-60.1 lets the Director satisfy valid court orders or judgments from the inmate trust account; 53.1-61 lets social services request withholding from work-release earnings for dependents on public assistance. 19.2-354 C also requires the facility, on request, to confirm hours worked and credits earned. 53.1-32.1 E lets the Director set pay incentives by difficulty and level of effort; 53.1-32.1 D makes prisoners who refuse a program assignment ineligible for good conduct allowances or earned sentence credits; 53.1-32.1 F says inmates employed under Article 2 are not state employees and are ineligible for Virginia Personnel Act benefits (2.2-2900 et seq.), unemployment benefits (60.2-600 et seq.) and workers' compensation (65.2-500 et seq.); 60.2-219 (27) also excludes inmate services for a penal or custodial institution from 'employment' for unemployment insurance. The death-sentence exception in 53.1-43.1 remains in the text although Virginia abolished capital punishment in 2021. Related charges and terms that are not core wage deductions: medical co-pay fees (53.1-32 A) and damaged-property recovery (53.1-228.1) charged to inmate accounts; in forma pauperis filing fees and costs paid in installments from the trust account (8.01-691); interest on invested prisoner funds used for prisoners generally, not credited to the individual (53.1-44); community corrections alternative program participants pay keep from employment earnings (19.2-316.4 D).
